config_name: Inner Being Analysis Programme — configuration seed
authority: researcher le Roux Cilliers; design = plan moonlit-launching-cocke.md (Appendix A/C)
status: IN-PROGRESS — foundational sections only; not yet loadable into a DB (loader + new DB not built)

meta.purpose: The config-level manifest AND the canonical definition of the rule envelope every config item carries. This is the ONE home for the shared envelope: each section file's meta describes only its own nodes and its own kind-specific `spec`, and refers here for `governs` / `kind` / `status` / `validation`. Do not restate these vocabularies in a section file — a second copy is how the same concept ends up defined four ways (the failure reconciliations.json exists to record).
meta.how_to_read: Every configuration item is a RULE with a fixed anatomy (plan A.10): a common envelope (defined below) + a kind-specific `spec` body (defined in that section's meta). The loader validates the envelope against this file and each `spec` against its section's spec-schema.

id.description: Stable unique code for the rule — the identifier the rest of the config and the runtime refer to it by. Dotted, kind-prefixed, never reused or renumbered once issued (e.g. `enum.role`, `dim.116.locus`, `recon.role-enum`).

governs.description: WHERE the rule is used — the process(es) AND/OR utility(ies) it applies to. A rule may govern more than one, and `all` is permitted for genuinely cross-cutting rules (provenance). This is the second query axis (plan A.11): asking for a process returns its full governing rule-set, which is what a module loads before it runs. NOTE (researcher ruling, 2026-07-15): `governs` does NOT decide tier. A Tier A (IBA-wide) rule is one where THE SAME RULE APPLIES IN ALL SITUATIONS — universality is the criterion — even though in practice it may only be used in some places, which is what `governs` records. So a wide rule legitimately carries a narrow `governs`.

kind.description: WHAT SORT of rule it is. Determines which section file houses it and which spec-schema its `spec` is validated against — kind and section are 1:1.

status.description: The rule's lifecycle state — whether it is the rule in force, a superseded one kept for provenance, or one whose value is contested and not yet decided.

version.description: Bumped on every change to the rule. A run is pinned to the config version it used, so a change is always traceable to the runs before and after it.

authority.description: WHERE IT COMES FROM — the decision or document the rule derives from (the rule's own provenance). A person + date for a researcher ruling, or a document for a written rule.

reference.description: WHERE IT IS FOUND — the doc §/`[current]` pointer where the rule is stated, so any rule can be read back to its source text. Distinct from `authority`: authority is who/what decided it, reference is where to go read it.

intent.description: HOW IT IS USED — what the rule means and why it exists (its semantics). The human-facing explanation; never a restatement of the `spec`.

satisfaction.description: WHEN IT IS TRUE — the pass condition, stated in plain words: what compliant data or a compliant process looks like. `validation` is the machine form of this.

validation.description: HOW IT IS ENFORCED — the check that decides satisfaction.

axis.description: Whether the check is deterministic code or needs the model. This is the [C]/[I] boundary the whole application turns on: [C] is enforced in code and the model can never override it; [I] is the only place the API is used.

check.description: The check to run, named. Currently free text naming the check (e.g. `value-in-domain`, `pair-direction driver->term`). ⚠ becomes a controlled vocabulary of named checks + parameters once the validation engine is built — see meta.open.check-vocabulary.

enum.description: For domain checks: the `enum.*` item id whose spec.values is the permitted domain. Must resolve to an item in enums.json (loader self-validation, plan A.5).

severity.description: What a failure does to the run.

enforcement.description: WHERE the control is enforced. The signalling node required by the researcher's ruling of 2026-07-15: the schema keeps regulating compliance with DB technology (CHECK · FK · NOT NULL · index), but those controls are SUBSERVIENT to the data-definition requirements defined here. A DB constraint is therefore a PROJECTION of a config rule, never a second definition of it — the configurator-maintenance utility reads this field, diffs config against the live schema, and raises the migration a config change requires. A hand-applied schema constraint on a config-governed control is a defect.

spec.description: The kind-specific body — the rule's actual content (an enum's values, a dimension's shape, a gate's check). Its schema is defined in the meta of the section file that houses this kind, and each kind is validated against its own schema.

vocab.governs.description: The study processes a rule can govern. These mirror the by-process rule-sets (plan A.11) and, roughly, the functional modules.

values.description: The initial word list: what qualifies a word as inner-being, the registry path, growth/addition policy, registry tags. ≈ module 2.
Retrieval from STEP: what to fetch, Strong's resolution and suffixes, the 60-cap sectioning, retry, cache-to-DB-first. ≈ module 1.
The raw data layer: what 'raw' is, its immutability, source-parity/completeness/no-null/FK controls, provenance stamping. ≈ module 1 output (the measure layer).
Verse and passage construction: the passage rule (char-continuity, anchor, no whole-chapter), verse coverage, genre routing, the candidate⇒verse-record invariant. ≈ module 3.

The per-term lexical decomposition layer: sense authority, the ve_nr dimension rules and ledgers, self-interpretable/never-ABSENT, grain, the stem master. ≈ module 5. RENAMED from `lexicon` on 2026-07-15 to end the collision with the raw Strong's-gloss `lexicon` entity (ent.raw.lexicon) — the PROCESS is `lexical`, the raw ENTITY is `lexicon`. Resolves meta.open.lexicon-naming on the filed recommendation; the collision had become an actual load failure across all three process files.
Screen 0, the candidate seed, the role model and per-role ledgers, ib_characteristic meaning-keying, the char-driven read. ≈ module 6.
Findings and observations: finding as the universal DB unit, STATED-vs-INFERRED, silence-is-a-finding, validity-by-convergence. ≈ module 9.

UTILITY. The sole write-path to the configurator: load · self-validate · version · edit · diff · rollback — and, per the 2026-07-15 ruling, diffing config against the live schema and raising the migration a config change requires.
UTILITY. The run interface, orchestrator and run manager: run plan, gate enforcement, tracking, checkpoints, resume, debug, errors.
UTILITY. Discovery/exploration over the corpus and the DB.
UTILITY. The DB access layer: single standard path, live-schema-aware, transactional, backup-aware.
UTILITY. The STEP client: local server, cache-to-DB-first.
UTILITY. Canonical morph-code / stem derivation.
UTILITY. The deterministic rule checker — every module's pre/post gate and the standalone validation battery.
UTILITY. The Claude API adapter — the ONLY place the API is used.
UTILITY. Programmatic commit/branch/push under the project's git discipline.
UTILITY. Filing, folders, archiving, versioning, and file-manifest maintenance — including the process index.
UTILITY. `.env` / secrets handling; never logged or exported.
Genuinely cross-cutting — applies to every process and utility alike (provenance, the behavioural guardrails).

vocab.governs.note: Two populations: the 7 STUDY PROCESSES (a process transforms study data) and the UTILITIES (`util.*` — a utility provides a capability). Per the 2026-07-15 ruling, a rule may govern either. The utility set is provisional — see meta.open.utility-set.

vocab.kind.description: The sort of rule. Each kind maps to exactly one section file and one spec-schema.

values.description: A controlled vocabulary — a word-group/lookup defined once, assigned a code, listing its permitted options.
A ve_nr lexical dimension: its shape, pair-direction, mandatoriness, derivability.
A genre × role mandatory-dimension set — which dimensions are required for a given genre and role.
A validation gate or measure: integrity invariants, content-validity, drift, coverage, acceptance-sample.
A functional pipeline module: its order, handler, enable flag, scope.
An edge in the module dependency graph: what a module needs first, and whether a missing prerequisite auto-activates or halts.
Standing methodological guidance (the nine principles, infer-don't-extract, convergence-validity). Governs how reads are done; mostly [I].
A naming/filing/label/patch/versioning pattern.
An operational parameter: model tier, DB path, thresholds, retries, budget caps, debug level.
A provenance or completion convention: markers, STATED-vs-INFERRED, completeness-as-validity, soft-delete discipline, field-authority.
A behavioural constraint drawn from the failure record that the app enforces (no-forced-structure, plausibility≠truth, resist-grouping, completeness≠validity).

A contested-value decision: one concept defined divergently across sources, needing ONE canonical value + an alias map. Carries its own decision-status vocabulary, not vocab.status — see wide/reconciliations.json meta.

A data entity a process owns — what it IS, its grain, its identity, what it holds, and which layer it belongs to. ADDED 2026-07-15 (the process files need it). ⚠ BOUNDARY: an entity item does NOT declare tables, columns or types — that is the schema's job (layout v2 §1). It says what the data MEANS; the schema says what structure holds it.
A human-facing artefact a process emits — projections, review packs, reports. Never authoritative: the DB is the source and every output is regenerable (plan §3.6). ADDED 2026-07-15.
A conditional routing rule — which treatment applies under which condition (genre routing being the live case). ADDED 2026-07-15; anticipated by plan A.3 cfg_route.

A rule governing an IBA utility rather than a study process. ADDED 2026-07-15 per the researcher's ruling that each utility gets its own json. Utility files are not yet authored — see meta.open.utility-set.

vocab.kind.nature_note: `nature` marks each kind DEFINITIONAL (it defines what a thing IS — enum, dimension, entity, output, reconciliation) or ENFORCEMENT (it constrains or wires — gate, module, dependency, route, pattern, setting, utility) or STANDING (principle, provenance, guardrail). Per the researcher's 2026-07-15 ruling, a definitional item defines the item, its options, and where it is used; HOW IT IS APPLIED is a separate enforcement rule with its own home. This is why `validation` is not-applicable on definitional kinds — see meta.open.definitional-kinds.
vocab.kind.open: `kind` is NO LONGER 1:1 with a file (layout v2 §2.2) — it selects the SPEC-SCHEMA; the file selects the process or utility. The `section` field is retired for the same reason. Still undefined: a kind for governance (GR-*/FLAG-*/interaction protocols). See meta.open.missing-kinds.

vocab.status.description: The lifecycle state of a rule. Applies to every item EXCEPT reconciliation items, which use their own decision-status vocabulary.

values.description: The current, authoritative rule. This is what the application enforces.
A superseded rule, kept for provenance and marked, never deleted — so old data and old reads remain interpretable. The application does not enforce it and must not write new data under it.

The concept is real but its VALUE is contested — the same rule is defined divergently across sources and the canonical form is not yet decided. A researcher decision, tracked in reconciliations.json. THE LOADER REFUSES TO RUN ANY STUDY MODULE THAT DEPENDS ON A RECONCILE RULE until it is resolved: a contested rule is a known-unknown, and running on one is how the study banked invalid data before. A RECONCILE item's `spec` may carry a working value plus its `variants`; the working value is NOT authority.

vocab.axis.description: How a rule is validated — the [C]/[I] boundary. Nearly every rule is [C]; only Screen 0, role assignment, and the semantic content of sense/operation/reading plus pair-bindings are genuinely [I] (plan §4).

values.description: Deterministic — checkable in code with no model involved (domain membership, shape, pair-direction, not-null, arithmetic, parity). Runs over the whole corpus in seconds, gives the same verdict every time, and CANNOT be overridden by the model. This is where the application's reliability comes from.

Interpretive — requires genuine inference, so the model produces it and a [C] gate then checks the output and retries on violation. The model never self-certifies: an [I] value that fails its [C] gate does not bank. Used only where the meaning genuinely cannot be derived mechanically.

⚠ PRESENT IN dimensions.json (`spec.derivation`) BUT NOT A VALID `validation.axis` VALUE. Means: morphology narrows the candidates but the choice still needs inference. Currently only ever appears as a derivation, never as an axis — see meta.open.axis-vs-derivation.

vocab.axis.note: `validation.axis` takes C or I only. `spec.derivation` on a dimension is a DIFFERENT field with an overlapping vocabulary (C · I · I-partial · read-only) — the two are not the same thing and must not be conflated. See meta.open.axis-vs-derivation.

vocab.enforcement.description: Where a control is actually enforced. Config is always the SOURCE of the rule; this says which mechanism carries it. Values prefixed `db:` are emitted and maintained in the schema BY the configurator-maintenance utility — the schema never authors them.

values.description: A CHECK constraint projects this rule (typically a domain drawn from an `enum.*` item).
A foreign key projects this rule (a referential invariant).
A NOT NULL constraint projects this rule (a mandatory-value rule).
An index projects this rule (a uniqueness or access requirement). Uniqueness invariants live here.
The validation engine enforces it. Everything a DB constraint cannot express: multi-table, conditional, arithmetic, distributional, or interpretive-output checks.
Both — the DB rejects the plainly-invalid, and a gate carries the part the constraint cannot express. Defence in depth for a red control.

vocab.enforcement.note: A rule whose enforcement is `db:*` still lives HERE in full. The constraint is downstream. See iba/docs/iba-configurator-layout-v2-20260715.md §1.1.

vocab.severity.description: What a failed check does to the run. Set per rule, enforced by the validation engine, recorded in app_validation_result.

values.description: HALT. A red pre-check refuses to run the module; a red post-check refuses to mark it done. Nothing that fails a red control banks. This is the mechanism behind 'done = validity, not coverage'.
Log and continue — flagged for human review, does not stop the run. The unit banks but carries an amber-review validity state and is queryable as such.

open.issue: `validation.check` is free text (e.g. 'value-in-domain', 'pair-direction driver->term', 'mandatory-not-absent + self-interpretable'). The same check is already phrased several ways, and compound checks are jammed into one string with '+'.
open.consequence: The validation engine cannot dispatch on free text, and drift between two phrasings of one check is undetectable.
open.resolve_by: A controlled vocabulary of named checks + typed parameters, decided when gates.json is authored (plan A.8 'how a gate's check_spec is stored').

open.issue: Two overlapping vocabularies: `validation.axis` (C|I) and dimension `spec.derivation` (C|I|I-partial|read-only). dim.103/105/107 declare derivation `I-partial`; dim.114/115 declare `read-only`, which is not an axis value at all.
open.consequence: 'How is this value produced' and 'how is this value checked' are different questions being answered with one blurred vocabulary.
open.resolve_by: Separate them explicitly: axis = how CHECKED (C|I); derivation = how PRODUCED (C|I|I-partial|read-only). Document derivation's vocabulary in dimensions.json meta. Researcher to confirm the split.

open.issue: Researcher ruling 2026-07-15: 'enums define the item, its options, and where it is used; HOW IT IS APPLIED is process configuration.' The ruling names a CAUSE — definitional rules conflated with enforcement rules — not merely an enum instance. dimensions.json has the same conflation and worse: every item carries a `validation` block, plus spec.rule (D3 driver-vs-restraint, D5 bearer!=God), spec.default (D117 literal) and spec.genre_note — all of which are 'how it is applied'.
open.consequence: Read consistently, a dimension defines ve_nr/label/shape/pair-endpoints/mandatory/derivation/enum ONLY, and every check on it becomes a gate in the lexical process's validation node: ~18 validation blocks removed, ~18 gates created.
open.recommendation: YES, it extends — leaving dimensions conflated reintroduces the very cause the ruling names. But the blast radius warrants confirming before acting.
open.resolve_by: researcher decision — BLOCKS authoring of process/lexical.json

open.issue: `validation` is a required envelope field, but a definitional item (an enum, post-ruling) has no validation of its own — the check enforcing its domain is a separate gate rule belonging to the field's process.
open.consequence: Every enum item currently carries a validation block it should not have, and the envelope as written forbids removing it.
open.recommendation: Make `validation` required only for ENFORCEMENT kinds (gate; plus whatever survives on dimension per meta.open.definitional-extends) and not-applicable for DEFINITIONAL kinds (enum). Mark each kind definitional-or-enforcement in vocab.kind.

open.issue: The researcher ruled that each IBA utility gets its own json (config maintenance, process run, discovery, etc.). The 11 `util.*` values now in vocab.governs are drawn from plan 3.3.1/3.3.3 but have not been confirmed as THE set.
open.consequence: The utility set decides how many config files exist and how `governs` is populated.
open.resolve_by: researcher confirmation of the list — BLOCKS authoring of the utility files

open.issue: `git` and `filing` were asked for as IBA-wide config files AND exist as utilities — but the 2026-07-15 ruling forbids one rule having two homes ('the entire rule for an entity must be defined in one place').
open.recommendation: They are UTILITY files; the wide layer cites them by id. The git rules ARE the git utility's configuration; the filing rules ARE the filing utility's.

open.issue: Kinds still undefined: `utility` (new, per the 2026-07-15 ruling) and genre routing (cfg_route). NOTE: kind is NO LONGER 1:1 with a file — the layout is now process-primary (layout v2 §2.2), so `kind` selects the SPEC-SCHEMA while the file selects the process or utility. The `section` field on each vocab.kind value is stale for the same reason.
open.resolve_by: Add kinds, and retire vocab.kind's `section` field, as the layout is applied.

open.issue: `lexicon` means two different things: the lexical-decomposition PROCESS (vocab.governs) and the Strong's-gloss raw TABLE. Flagged in the plan (A.11) and still unreconciled.
open.consequence: 'lexicon rules' is ambiguous in exactly the layer that failed validation.
open.resolve_by: Rename one. Candidate: the process becomes `lexical`, the raw table keeps `lexicon`. Researcher decision.

open.issue: The config's own vocabularies (vocab.governs/kind/status/axis/severity) are defined HERE in prose-ish JSON, not as `enum.*` items in enums.json — yet they are word-groups with codes, which is exactly what enums.json is for.
open.consequence: Two homes for 'what is a controlled vocabulary in this system'.
open.resolve_by: Decide whether the config self-hosts (its own vocabularies become enum items, loader bootstraps from them) or whether meta-vocabularies are deliberately held apart as the envelope's own definition. Researcher decision — affects the loader.

layout.shape: Two tiers. TIER A (wide/) = rules where THE SAME RULE APPLIES IN ALL SITUATIONS, plus one file per UTILITY. TIER B (process/) = one file per study process, with facets as NODES (process · entities · output · validation · naming · filing), not as separate files.
layout.note: The file layout is authoring ergonomics, not architecture — at runtime every rule is a row carrying `kind` + `governs`, queryable on both axes regardless of which file authored it. The researcher's observation stands: consolidated into the DB, these plausibly become ONE table (see meta.open.rule-table). Files may therefore be re-cut cheaply; the envelope may not.
layout.state: TRANSITIONAL — the 4 authored files still sit in the flat pre-ruling layout at config/ root. Nothing has been moved.
